ChatRequest.description:
`messages` are the NEW turns only; for an existing conversation the server prepends
its stored history before calling the model.

`provider`/`model` pick who should answer (docs/25-openrouter.md). Both may be omitted:
an existing conversation keeps its own, a new one gets the server default (OpenRouter's
default model when it is usable, else the local default). A `model` without a
`provider` means OpenRouter only when it is one of the allowed OpenRouter ids.
`context` links a conversation to finance/trading/research (forces local inference);
a link only ever gets stricter.

never deployed: merging a PR stays behind the approval gate.

post.description:
201 with the new intent (already risk-checked: PENDING_RISK or REJECTED), or 200 with
the existing one when this correlation_id was already used for the same request.

Backward-compatible wrapper over the approval engine. Files (or reuses) the pending
`trading.paper_intent` request for this intent. With {"password"} and a policy needing a
single approval, approves it now: 200 with the intent (FILLED, SUBMITTED or REJECTED by
risk). Otherwise 202 with the approval id, to approve from the inbox.

password: a policy can switch re-auth off. Pending requests keep the policy they were
filed under.

schema.title: Response Put Policies Api V1 Approvals Policies Put

post.description:
Verify the password once and stamp this login session (server-side, in Redis). Requests
whose policy has reauth_max_age_seconds > 0 can then be approved with
{"use_reauth": true} while the stamp is young enough.

get.description:
SSE: one `approval` event per approval state change (see app/services/
approval_stream.py). Resumes after `Last-Event-ID` or `?last_event_id=`.

With `check_drift=true` the artifacts of a pending request are recomputed now (this may
call GitHub) and compared with what was filed.

post.description:
Re-authenticates (the password, or this session's re-auth stamp when the policy accepts
one), counts the approval and, once the policy's quorum is reached, executes. 200 with
status `pending` (more approvals needed), `executed` or `failed`; 409 when expired,
already used, already approved by you or invalidated by drift; 403 on a wrong or missing
re-auth (audited) or a refused self-approval.

get.description:
The events in order and the hash-chain verification (`chain.status` ok | broken |
legacy | empty).

Host deploys (`deployer` agent runs) and GitHub Actions CI runs, newest first. DB only:
never calls GitHub (the webhook worker and the sync job keep the runs fresh).
